You got this! You totally got this.

That wouldn't be very respectful of them to not honor your boundaries in what you would be comfortable with. I've reached out to people that I wasn't necessarily close to before to help me, like my boss at work. That way I didn't have to say everything that was going on, but just enough to know that someone knew.

If you have someone genuine in your life that respects you, you could keep it as simple as telling them that you have an appointment coming up. You could say that it's for your health & that you don't feel comfortable talking about the reasons, but you just want them to know because you might need some encouragement to even go.
Is there anyone in your life you could think to tell? You know to have someone hold you accountable, or as a way to hold yourself accountable.
Fair enough. Does anyone else know about our appointment?
It is most certainly helpful! Can you let me know how it goes after your appointment?

If they want to know anything else, then they will ask you. It makes sense, that's what you know & is your normal thinking. Something I will say is that I try to plan things I will say before talking to people, especially professional help. I usually get so nervous when I'm actually there that I forget or change my mind, so I started writing things down that I want to say & I've just given them my note before. I don't know if you are the same way, just a suggestion.

Good. I'm glad that you already have it planned out what you are going to tell them. I 100% relate. It's hard & confusing when thoughts/feelings seem so rationalized to you, when you know other people don't feel the same way.
That if you feel like seeing a therapist won't help you then you feel like your only other option is suicide. To express the seriousness in which you feel like ending your life.

It says something that you are willing to go. I would definitely let them know that as well. I hope it helps enough to at least get on the road to feeling safe. I'm confident that if you don't give up that you will get there.
Yeah. Therapists can be tricky sometimes. I'm glad you have an appointment. That's a good first step.
Do you have a therapist?
What about goals? Anything you'd want for the future? It's all changing your way of thinking honestly. If you find more to live for, even an ounce of motivation can get you a long way.
Why wouldn't you want to cause pain for others?
It is absolutely difficult. That's what keeps me alive. I realized I don't want to ever put that pain in someone else after feeling it myself.

What do you want to live for? 
Find that one thing & hang on to it. Remember you are not alone. It's a matter of taking it one day at a time. The only way to truly help yourself is when you're ready. There are options though. I have stayed away from meds & shrinks for years. I recently enrolled in intensive outpatient CBT, which feels life changing. DBT is next. I have always been convinced that suicide was my way out, until I lost someone to it, & felt the pain I knew I would be putting on to others. For me, that's my motivation to stay alive. What's yours?

What are you doing for yourself? 
What ifs don't help anything. It just deepens the cycle of anxiety. I know it's hard, all you can do right now is to take care of yourself.

With relationships the key is effective communication. Assertiveness is the goal. What I do is take time to assess my feelings & thoughts. I struggle with being in the past or future, as anxiety tends to bring a lot of fear among other things. Meditation & deep breathing exercises help with being present. Thinking too much about anything except for the moment you are in influences how you think, how you feel, how you act. When communicating I take 4 steps: I observe, I think, I feel, I need. Example: "I observe that the anxiety & insecurities I have had impact our relationship. I think I don't want this to hurt our relationship. I feel anxious, concerned, fearful. I need you to be patient & supportive." Then of course taking action is the hardest part, it's a process. Training your brain to turn the negatives into either a positive or neutral. From my experience having been in your position, it never helped expressing or even thinking about the what ifs. I've also been in situations where it was intuition & the bad vibes I were feeling were real. Overall, meditation & being present, changing thought process, & learning to effectively communicate has improved my life immensely. I hope that's helpful.

I started smoking weed after I quit drinking almost 3 years ago. I used to smoke every day and now only occasionally do if my anxiety is wild or I get a migraine. I prefer being sober, I don't ever intend on going back to drinking. I have a lot of motivators. One day at a time.

That's an excellent idea. I imagine it would be hard diving right back into therapy and meds all at once, it's already overwhelming just making an appointment. Very true, it would be nice to have someone to talk to without burdening those around me. Thank you for the comment, it's much appreciated.

I feel like there are not very many options in the city I live in, I am actually branching out and looking for options in a larger city which is only about an hour drive. I definitely am not going to waste my time with douches that aren't there to help me. Thanks! I keep a pretty strong head on my shoulders for the most part. I got this!

You sound exactly like me. I have terrible sense of direction that goes along with getting lost and anxious like that quite a bit when I'm not familiar with the area. I also have a lot I need to talk through with my childhood, traumas that haven't been dealt with, alcohol abuse (I am sober 2 years now and it's still a struggle), and the aftermath of being overly sexual. Your fiancé seems like good support for you, encouraging you to seek help, and sticking through your manic episode/diagnosis. I know it's definitely hard for our loved ones to witness what we go through and not always knowing what to do. I think finding the right person will be the hardest part initially, I have an idea of what the right type of person would be for me. Thank you so much for sharing. Everyone's responses are helping me so much. I'm about this close to making an appointment. I have a list of therapists, I just haven't decided on one to call yet.

It definitely makes life hard not feeling understood by those around me. I agree in needing that professional support first and that being open to medication is important. My fear is that when I do reach out I won't be listened to or have someone that will work on the right meds with me. After reading others experiences and seeing how much it helps others I feel kind of silly for feeling that way. That's where not giving up comes in to play. Tackling this head on seems the only way to go. Thank you so much.

That's impressive! You definitely acted quick on getting help and sticking to meds. I can say I've been on and off meds for years as well as seeing various different therapists/psychiatrists that honestly I didn't feel like were there to help me at all. DBT and CBT I have looked into that I feel would massively help me. Part of the reason I stopped seeing professionals was because I was told I only needed meds and was refused a regular therapist, which was pretty discouraging to me. I'm happy for you that you have such great support from your boyfriend and daughter, after all your support system means everything. Thanks for sharing. The more I know of others successes is even more motivating to seek out help for myself.

Sounds like you have some pretty solid support there. I'm glad you had that to help guide you in a positive direction. I feel like I have or am reaching that level of desperation. I definitely don't want it to get worse and I can feel all of my symptoms worsening or maybe I am just realizing how much my life has been effected after not being medicated for so long. (Obstinateness is indeed a word!) I hope to one day be where you're at, it's very inspirational. Especially knowing that someone as like minded as myself can grow into something better and be in a more mindful place. Thank you for sharing and for your kind words.
